title: Subtract the opening once
hook: A rectangular panel includes a 2m² opening. Counting the outline counts too much surface.

knows: that a model can declare hypothetical quantities
doesNotKnow: Subtract a stated opening from rectangular coverage area.

misconception: The outer rectangle always equals the area requiring material.
objective: Subtract a stated opening from rectangular coverage area.

claims.text: An ideal panel is 3m high and 4m wide, with one 2m² opening that needs no covering. Scaled model; ideal dimensions; fixed 2m² opening.
claims.source: Declared hypothetical inputs and limits in resource-specs.json. No actual product, price, tariff, shelf-life, treatment or physical appliance specification is asserted.

claims.text: The stage's two results are computed by the printed expressions. At Width=4m, A=10m² and B=12m². The geometry pictures follow the declared dimension relationships; other stage pictures are scaled to the larger displayed comparison and icons are not literal item counts.
claims.source: src/lib/lifehacks/resource-specs.json contains this lesson's numeric AST; src/lib/lifehacks/resource-model.ts evaluates it. A=["-",["*","x",3],2]; B=["*","x",3]; x denotes Width. At x=4, A=10, B=12; recall at x=7: B=21. Values are fictional/ideal assumptions, not measurements. Display rounds to at most three decimals.

claims.text: Multiply width by height for the outline, then subtract the opening’s area once. The outline is a boundary enclosing both material and empty space; it is not automatically the area needing coverage.
claims.source: src/lib/lifehacks/resource-specs.json contains this lesson's numeric AST; src/lib/lifehacks/resource-model.ts evaluates it. A=["-",["*","x",3],2]; B=["*","x",3]; x denotes Width. The principle follows from those expressions and stated scenario limits.

claims.text: An ideal panel is 3m high and 4m wide, with one 2m² opening that needs no covering. Change only Width to 7m. What is B (Outline) now? Correct: 21m². Use B's stated rule with Width=7m: it gives 21m². Multiply width by height for the outline, then subtract the opening’s area once. The outline is a boundary enclosing both material and empty space; it is not automatically the area needing coverage.

recall.question: An ideal panel is 3m high and 4m wide, with one 2m² opening that needs no covering. Change only Width to 7m. What is B (Outline) now?
recall.why: Use B's stated rule with Width=7m: it gives 21m². Multiply width by height for the outline, then subtract the opening’s area once. The outline is a boundary enclosing both material and empty space; it is not automatically the area needing coverage.
